scenes.text: You probably know that a great white shark can smell a single drop of blood in a massive swimming pool, but did you know that your own nose actually possesses a superpower that makes sharks look completely nose-blind?
There is a specific earthy scent called geosmin, which is an organic compound released by soil microbes the exact moment rain hits the dry ground.

Humans are so incredibly sensitive to this rain aroma that we can detect it at just five parts per trillion, meaning you are literally two hundred thousand times more sensitive to wet soil than a shark is to blood in the ocean.
Why do you think evolution gave us this bizarre survival superpower, and would you follow us to uncover more secrets?
